suggested_services_note: Each row is one way this kind of work takes money (one of the master's 28 paths per flow). The owner keeps the services that fit and picks ONE path per service and place. Names and amounts are examples from the profession file, not prices.

suggested_services.name: Wedding consultation
suggested_services.example: The main story: a free 45-minute wedding consultation with Elliot at the shop. Nothing is taken: a YES books it, and nothing is paid after.

suggested_services.name: Everyday arrangement
suggested_services.example: A $55 everyday arrangement picked up at the shop, paid in full when ordered.

suggested_services.name: Courthouse wedding set
suggested_services.example: A $140 courthouse wedding set (a bouquet and 2 boutonnieres) picked up Saturday: a $40 deposit now, and the $100 rest paid at pickup, at the counter.

suggested_services.name: Anniversary brunch flowers
suggested_services.example: The main story: flowers for Alex's parents' anniversary brunch at Maple Hall, quoted from the plan at $640 (over $500, so Sam OKs it). Both sign the contract. A $160 deposit now, and the $480 rest on the bill after the event.

suggested_services.name: Sympathy arrangement, delivered
suggested_services.example: A $150 sympathy arrangement for Alex's aunt's service, delivered to Brookside Funeral Home before 11am, paid in full when ordered. Everyday deliveries go the same way.

before_times: An event: the date, the venue's town, how many tables or guests, the colors, and a flower budget if there is one
A sympathy order: the day and time of the service, and the funeral home
An everyday order: the occasion, and pickup or delivery
A consultation: a wedding or another event, and about how many guests
after_time: The venue's rules: setup and pickup times, open flame, what can hang
The wedding party: bouquets and boutonnieres
The card message for a delivery
secure_page_only: Allergy details, like flowers to avoid
The name for a sympathy card, and the name of the person who died
A recipient's address and phone (the recipient gets no texts)
The venue's contact for the day
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older). A teen asks a parent to order. Anyone may order for another adult, as a gift, and pay for it. A company may pay for an event (B4-35).

safety_and_stop_words.what_rosie_says: Danger now: get everyone out, and call 911. No booking until it's safe. A candle fire that's already out gets the safety steps first, then the booking goes on: keep candles away from the flowers, and call 911 if smoke comes back.

first_steps_and_forms.prep: The venue's side door or loading door open at the setup time; candles in glass. For a consultation: bring photos you love, and the venue's rules if you have them.

staff.skills: Luca leads quoted events and does plant care. Felix does sympathy pieces, deliveries and setups. Elliot leads consultations and custom pieces at the shop, and Hazel does everyday work at the counter.
staff.licenses_or_certificates: Designers hold no license of their own. Plant techs hold an applicator license where the state's rules require one (Luca; Reese, who joins later).
staff.who_oks: Sam OKs every wedding and every quote over $500. Pat may OK Lee Floral Design prices over $500; Sam's answer wins.
staff.stand_in: For an event on a date that can't move: a lead designer Sam trusts from outside the team (Petra Lund), or a full refund.
staff.crews: A large setup may need two designers and the van.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older). A teen asks a parent to order. Anyone may order for another adult, as a gift, and pay for it. A company may pay for an event (B4-35).

visit.check_in: An event: the code at the venue's door, from whoever meets the designer (the customer, or the venue's contact for the day). A consultation: the code at the shop's desk, or read out at the start by video. A pickup: the code at the counter. A delivery to a funeral home, an office or a recipient: no code; DONE with a photo, and the sender gets the photo.
visit.done: DONE with photos of the setup. Loaned vases are counted at pickup, at the time the venue set. A missing one is a fee only with Sam's yes.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Floral design and a flower shop: no state license in most places. The business registration, and a seller's permit for sales tax where the state's form asks for one. Plant care that treats plants for pests: a pest control license for the company and an applicator license for each plant tech, where the state's rules require them. All from the state's form.
license.who: The business holds its registration, any seller's permit and any pest control license. Each plant tech holds their own applicator license. Designers hold no license of their own.
ask: The seller's permit number, where the state's form asks for one
The company's pest control license, if it treats plants for pests
Each plant tech's applicator license, in their invite reply
license.insurance: Liability insurance on file, with its end date. Many venues ask for a certificate naming them before setup (B4-70).
license.background: Only where the state's form asks.

never_in_a_text: The name of the person who died
